- Root cause: the comment's premise is wrong. `task_workflow._load_registry()` does `registry_path().read_text()` fresh on EVERY call — it is uncached (`task_workflow.py:547-551`), so the rewritten registry `path` is always re-read regardless. - Why this is Minor, not a blocker: it is (a) NOT a test smell hiding a bug — the test passes for the right reason both ways (the production guard catches the raise; the pre-fix proof above confirms it fails without the fix); (b) NOT a leak of test isolation into production code — `invalidate_cache()` is a legitimate public `task_workflow` helper the fixture itself already calls at setup (`:167`), invoked here only from test code. It is a harmless dead line + a misleading comment. Suggested fix (optional, non-blocking): drop the line, or correct the comment to note `_load_registry` is uncached so no bust is required. Plan v2 § "Plan deviations: allowed without asking" covers adding it; the deviation is in-bounds, just unnecessary.
- Mechanizable: no (judgment about whether a no-op line + comment is worth keeping; not a mechanical-verifier candidate).
